nightly_cleanup.title: Nightly code cleanup
nightly_cleanup.desc: Nightly sweep for quality issues — dead code, duplicated logic, stale comments, security risks — fixes are left UNCOMMITTED: the run stops and waits for human review; code is committed only after you confirm.
nightly_cleanup.prompt:
Nightly code cleanup (unattended + human review):
1. Read through the workspace codebase (use git log to spot recent hotspots) and audit against quality standards: dead code and unused exports, duplicated logic, naming/structure issues, overly long functions, missing error handling, leftover TODO/FIXMEs, redundant or misleading comments, obvious security risks (hardcoded secrets, injection, unreleased resources).
2. Only fix "high-confidence + low-risk" issues: keep each change small and revertible, run the project lint/tests after each change, and immediately revert any change that breaks tests.
3. Do NOT run git commit or git push in this round: leave all changes in the working tree, then stop and output a morning report — suggested fixes (file path + what changed + verification result) and items deliberately left alone (with reasons), and wait for human review.
4. A human will review and respond in this session. Only when they explicitly ask you to commit, group the changes into commits by issue type (message explains motivation and scope; still do not push).
